detailed_results.query: Can you give me a breakdown by building of how many records fall into each electricity usage category, along with the average, total, and highest grid electricity consumption for each building, and show that alongside their multifamily water efficiency score plus the counts of financial-office computers and any other computers per building, grouped by data center gross floor area and worship facility gross floor?
detailed_results.sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (SELECT t1.property_id_1, t3.property_id_1, t3.electricity_use_grid_purchase_2, t3.water_score_multifamily_only, t5.financial_office_computer, t5.other_computer_density_number, CASE WHEN t3.electricity_use_grid_purchase_2 > 1000000 THEN 'High usage' WHEN t3.electricity_use_grid_purchase_2 > 500000 THEN 'Medium usage' ELSE 'Low usage' END as category, t2.data_center_gross_floor_area, t4.worship_facility_gross_floor FROM `Energy and Water Data Disclosure for Local Law 84 2018 (Data for Calendar Year 2017)_nyc_energy_water_usage_2017` t1
INNER JOIN `Energy and Water Data Disclosure for Local Law 84 2018 (Data for Calendar Year 2017)_nyc_energy_water_disclosure_2017_1` t2 ON t1.property_id = t2.property_id
INNER JOIN `Energy and Water Data Disclosure for Local Law 84 2018 (Data for Calendar Year 2017)_energy_water_usage_2017` t3 ON t1.property_id_1 = t3.property_id_1
INNER JOIN `Energy and Water Data Disclosure for Local Law 84 2018 (Data for Calendar Year 2017)_nyc_building_energy_water_2017` t4 ON t2.property_name = t4.property_name
INNER JOIN `Energy and Water Data Disclosure for Local Law 84 2018 (Data for Calendar Year 2017)_nyc_energy_water_disclosure_2017` t5 ON t4.address_1 = t5.address_1 WHERE t3.electricity_use_grid_purchase_2 IS NOT NULL) SELECT property_id_1, water_score_multifamily_only, financial_office_computer, other_computer_density_number, category, COUNT(*) as count, AVG(electricity_use_grid_purchase_2) as avg_value, SUM(electricity_use_grid_purchase_2) as total_value, MAX(electricity_use_grid_purchase_2) as max_value FROM categorized_data GROUP BY property_id_1, water_score_multifamily_only, financial_office_computer, other_computer_density_number, category, data_center_gross_floor_area, worship_facility_gross_floor

INNER JOIN `Energy and Water Data Disclosure for Local Law 84 2018 (Data for Calendar Year 2017)_nyc_building_energy_water_2017` t4 ON t2.property_name = t4.property_name
INNER JOIN `Energy and Water Data Disclosure for Local Law 84 2018 (Data for Calendar Year 2017)_nyc_energy_water_disclosure_2017` t5 ON t4.address_1 = t5.address_1 GROUP BY t3.property_id_1, postcode, data_center_gross_floor_area, worship_facility_gross_floor, weather_normalized_site_energy

    t1.property_id_1,

  INNER JOIN `Energy and Water Data Disclosure for Local Law 84 2018 (Data for Calendar Year 2017)_nyc_energy_water_disclosure_2017` t5 ON t4.address_1 = t5.address_1

detailed_results.query: Can you show me, for each building and its street address, how many records fall into each water‑use category (like low, medium, or high), along with the average, total, and highest water use intensity for those buildings, grouped by postcode as well?
detailed_results.sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (SELECT t2.property_name, t4.property_name, t4.address_1, t5.address_1, t3.electricity_use_grid_purchase_2, t4.water_use_intensity_all_water, t5.water_current_date, CASE WHEN t4.water_use_intensity_all_water > 200 THEN 'High water intensity' WHEN t4.water_use_intensity_all_water > 100 THEN 'Medium water intensity' ELSE 'Low water intensity' END as category, t1.postcode FROM `Energy and Water Data Disclosure for Local Law 84 2018 (Data for Calendar Year 2017)_nyc_energy_water_usage_2017` t1
INNER JOIN `Energy and Water Data Disclosure for Local Law 84 2018 (Data for Calendar Year 2017)_nyc_energy_water_disclosure_2017_1` t2 ON t1.property_id = t2.property_id
INNER JOIN `Energy and Water Data Disclosure for Local Law 84 2018 (Data for Calendar Year 2017)_energy_water_usage_2017` t3 ON t1.property_id_1 = t3.property_id_1
INNER JOIN `Energy and Water Data Disclosure for Local Law 84 2018 (Data for Calendar Year 2017)_nyc_building_energy_water_2017` t4 ON t2.property_name = t4.property_name
INNER JOIN `Energy and Water Data Disclosure for Local Law 84 2018 (Data for Calendar Year 2017)_nyc_energy_water_disclosure_2017` t5 ON t4.address_1 = t5.address_1 WHERE t4.water_use_intensity_all_water IS NOT NULL) SELECT property_name, address_1, category, COUNT(*) as count, AVG(water_use_intensity_all_water) as avg_value, SUM(water_use_intensity_all_water) as total_value, MAX(water_use_intensity_all_water) as max_value FROM categorized_data GROUP BY property_name, address_1, category, postcode

detailed_results.query: Could you give me a list of the top 100 buildings, showing their name and street address, along with how much electricity they’re using from the grid in total, how many underlying records that total is based on, and the average usage per record, but only for places where the total usage is above zero and where there’s also information about office computer energy use in the same location?
detailed_results.sql:
WITH base_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t1.property_id,
    t1.property_id_1,
    t2.property_id,
    t2.property_name,
    t3.property_id_1 AS t3_property_id_1,
    t4.property_name AS t4_property_name,
    t4.address_1,
    t5.address_1 AS t5_address_1,
    t3.electricity_use_grid_purchase_2,
    t5.financial_office_computer
  FROM `Energy and Water Data Disclosure for Local Law 84 2018 (Data for Calendar Year 2017)_nyc_energy_water_usage_2017` t1
  INNER JOIN `Energy and Water Data Disclosure for Local Law 84 2018 (Data for Calendar Year 2017)_nyc_energy_water_disclosure_2017_1` t2 ON t1.property_id = t2.property_id
  INNER JOIN `Energy and Water Data Disclosure for Local Law 84 2018 (Data for Calendar Year 2017)_energy_water_usage_2017` t3 ON t1.property_id_1 = t3.property_id_1
  INNER JOIN `Energy and Water Data Disclosure for Local Law 84 2018 (Data for Calendar Year 2017)_nyc_building_energy_water_2017` t4 ON t2.property_name = t4.property_name
  INNER JOIN `Energy and Water Data Disclosure for Local Law 84 2018 (Data for Calendar Year 2017)_nyc_energy_water_disclosure_2017` t5 ON t4.address_1 = t5.address_1
  WHERE t3.electricity_use_grid_purchase_2 IS NOT NULL
), aggregated AS (
  SELECT 
    property_name,
    address_1,
    SUM(electricity_use_grid_purchase_2) AS total,
    COUNT(*) AS count,
    AVG(electricity_use_grid_purchase_2) AS average
  FROM base_data
  GROUP BY property_name, address_1
)
SELECT 
  property_name,
  address_1,
  total,
  count,
  average
FROM aggregated
WHERE total > 0
ORDER BY total DESC
LIMIT 100

   - If you select `table_name_1`, you MUST also check and include `table_name`, `table_name_2`, `table_name_3`, etc.

   - `records` and `records_1` and `records_2` are THREE DIFFERENT tables

detailed_results.query: Can you show me, for each building and its related record, how many sign applications there are, along with the average, total, and highest estimated fees, broken down by the building number, current job status, the most recent date any action was taken, fee category (high/medium/low based on estimated fee thresholds), payment status, and special district name—only including records where the job actually has a status?
detailed_results.sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (
  SELECT t1.bin__, t3.bin__, t1.total_est_fee, t1.owner_type, t3.job_status, t5.latest_action_date,
         CASE
           WHEN t1.total_est_fee > 1000 THEN 'high'
           WHEN t1.total_est_fee > 100 THEN 'medium'
           ELSE 'low'
         END AS category, t2.paid, t4.special_dist_name
  FROM `node_1` t1
  INNER JOIN `DOB Sign Application Filings_sign_application_records` t2 ON t1.job__ = t2.job__
  INNER JOIN `node_3` t3 ON t1.bin__ = t3.bin__
  INNER JOIN `DOB Sign Application Filings_sign_application_records_1` t4 ON t2.block = t4.block
  INNER JOIN `DOB Sign Application Filings_sign_application_details` t5 ON t4.owner_s__phone__ = t5.owner_s__phone__
  WHERE t3.job_status IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT bin__, job_status, latest_action_date, category,
       COUNT(*) AS count,
       AVG(total_est_fee) AS avg_value,
       SUM(total_est_fee) AS total_value,
       MAX(total_est_fee) AS max_value
FROM categorized_data
GROUP BY bin__, job_status, latest_action_date, category, paid, special_dist_name

detailed_results.query: Can you pull a breakdown of sign-related jobs where there are at least five matching records, grouped by each job number and building identifier (from both the main filing and the sign application), special district name, and for each group show whether it's for advertising signage, the current status of the job, the most recent action date, and the record count along with the total, average, highest, and lowest estimated fees?
detailed_results.sql:
WITH base_data AS (SELECT t1.job__ AS t1_job__, t2.job__ AS t2_job__, t1.bin__ AS t1_bin__, t3.bin__ AS t3_bin__, t1.total_est_fee, t1.initial_cost, t2.sign_advertising, t3.job_status, t5.latest_action_date, t4.special_dist_name FROM `node_1` t1
INNER JOIN `DOB Sign Application Filings_sign_application_records` t2 ON t1.job__ = t2.job__
INNER JOIN `node_3` t3 ON t1.bin__ = t3.bin__
INNER JOIN `DOB Sign Application Filings_sign_application_records_1` t4 ON t2.block = t4.block
INNER JOIN `DOB Sign Application Filings_sign_application_details` t5 ON t4.owner_s__phone__ = t5.owner_s__phone__ WHERE t1.total_est_fee IS NOT NULL) SELECT t1_job__, t2_job__, t1_bin__, t3_bin__, sign_advertising, job_status, latest_action_date, COUNT(*) as record_count, SUM(total_est_fee) as total_amount, AVG(total_est_fee) as avg_amount, MAX(total_est_fee) as max_amount, MIN(total_est_fee) as min_amount FROM base_data GROUP BY t1_job__, t2_job__, t1_bin__, t3_bin__, sign_advertising, job_status, latest_action_date, special_dist_name HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5

detailed_results.query: Can you show me, for each sign owner, their three most recent jobs based on latest action date, including when the job first went into the system, the current job status along with its description in plain language, the owner's phone number, the date of the latest action taken on each job, whether the sign is located close to a highway, the rank of each job by latest action date within each owner, the dense rank of each job by latest action date within each job status, the total estimated fee, and the amount paid?
detailed_results.sql:
WITH ranked AS (
  SELECT 
    t3.dobrundate,
    t3.job_status,
    t4.owner_s__phone__,
    t4.job_status_descrp,
    t5.owner_s__phone__,
    t5.latest_action_date,
    t5.sign_near_highway,
    RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY t4.owner_s__phone__ ORDER BY t5.latest_action_date DESC) as rank,
    DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY t3.job_status ORDER BY t5.latest_action_date) as dense_rank, t1.total_est_fee, t2.paid
  FROM `node_1` t1
  INNER JOIN `DOB Sign Application Filings_sign_application_records` t2 ON t1.job__ = t2.job__
  INNER JOIN `node_3` t3 ON t1.bin__ = t3.bin__
  INNER JOIN `DOB Sign Application Filings_sign_application_records_1` t4 ON t2.block = t4.block
  INNER JOIN `DOB Sign Application Filings_sign_application_details` t5 ON t4.owner_s__phone__ = t5.owner_s__phone__
)
SELECT 
  dobrundate,
  job_status,
  owner_s__phone__,
  job_status_descrp,
  latest_action_date,
  sign_near_highway,
  rank,
  dense_rank, total_est_fee, paid
FROM ranked
WHERE rank <= 3

detailed_results.query: Can you show me, for each pair of nearby blocks where sign applications are linked together by the same owner's phone number, how many signs there are by construction type and weight category, along with the average, total, and maximum sign weight for each of those block and owner combinations, grouped by total estimated fee?
detailed_results.sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t2.block AS t2_block,
    t4.block AS t4_block,
    t4.owner_s__phone__ AS t4_owner_phone,
    t5.owner_s__phone__ AS t5_owner_phone,
    t3.sign_const_type,
    t5.sign_weight,
    CASE 
      WHEN t5.sign_weight > 1000 THEN 'heavy'
      WHEN t5.sign_weight > 500 THEN 'medium'
      ELSE 'light'
    END as category, t1.total_est_fee
  FROM `node_1` t1
  INNER JOIN `DOB Sign Application Filings_sign_application_records` t2 ON t1.job__ = t2.job__
  INNER JOIN `node_3` t3 ON t1.bin__ = t3.bin__
  INNER JOIN `DOB Sign Application Filings_sign_application_records_1` t4 ON t2.block = t4.block
  INNER JOIN `DOB Sign Application Filings_sign_application_details` t5 ON t4.owner_s__phone__ = t5.owner_s__phone__
  WHERE t5.sign_weight IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
  t2_block,
  t4_block,
  t4_owner_phone,
  t5_owner_phone,
  sign_const_type,
  category,
  COUNT(*) as count,
  AVG(sign_weight) as avg_value,
  SUM(sign_weight) as total_value,
  MAX(sign_weight) as max_value
FROM categorized_data
GROUP BY 
  t2_block,
  t4_block,
  t4_owner_phone,
  t5_owner_phone,
  sign_const_type,
  category, total_est_fee

detailed_results.query: Can you show me the top ten building permits for each type of work ordered by census tract (highest first), including the job ID, what kind of permit it is, the category of work being done, the current status of the permit, the census tract where it's located, any more specific subtype or classification of the permit, the neighborhood name, whether each one is for a residential property, the permit sequence number, and the job type, filtered to only show permits with an 'ISSUED' status?
detailed_results.sql:
WITH ranked_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t3.job__,
    t3.permit_type,
    t3.work_type,
    t4.permit_status,
    t4.gis_census_tract,
    t5.permit_subtype,
    t5.gis_nta_name,
    t5.residential,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t3.work_type ORDER BY t4.gis_census_tract DESC) as row_num, t1.permit_sequence__, t2.job_type
  FROM `DOB Permit Issuance_building_permit_issuance` t1
  INNER JOIN `DOB Permit Issuance_building_permit_issuance_2` t2 ON t1.permit_si_no = t2.permit_si_no
  INNER JOIN `DOB Permit Issuance_building_permit_issuance_1` t3 ON t1.job__ = t3.job__
  INNER JOIN `DOB Permit Issuance_permit_issuance_records_1` t4 ON t1.bin__ = t4.bin__
  INNER JOIN `DOB Permit Issuance_permit_issuance_records` t5 ON t2.gis_longitude = t5.gis_longitude
  WHERE t4.permit_status = 'ISSUED'
)
SELECT 
  job__,
  permit_type,
  work_type,
  permit_status,
  gis_census_tract,
  permit_subtype,
  gis_nta_name,
  residential, permit_sequence__, job_type
FROM ranked_data
WHERE row_num <= 10

detailed_results.query: Could you show me the top ten records per original contract expiration date, ordered by the highest permit or license charge within each group, and for each one include the minimum fees that were set for March, June, August, and February, along with the date when the permit or license ends, the original contract expiration date, and the operator status, but only in cases where the permit or license end date is actually filled in?
detailed_results.sql:
WITH ranked_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t3.permitorlicensefee,
    t3.marchminfee,
    t4.juneminfee,
    t4.permitorlicenseenddate,
    t5.augustminfee,
    t5.origcontracexpdate,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY t5.origcontracexpdate 
      ORDER BY t3.permitorlicensefee DESC
    ) AS row_num, t1.operatorstatus, t2.februaryminfee
  FROM `Parks Concessions_park_concession_contracts` t1
  INNER JOIN `node_2` t2 ON t1.contractcode = t2.contractcode
  INNER JOIN `Parks Concessions_park_concession_fees` t3 ON t1.personid = t3.personid
  INNER JOIN `Parks Concessions_concession_contracts_info` t4 ON t1.operatorlastname = t4.operatorlastname
  INNER JOIN `Parks Concessions_concession_contracts_details` t5 ON t2.addlocationinfo1 = t5.addlocationinfo1
  WHERE t4.permitorlicenseenddate IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
  permitorlicensefee,
  marchminfee,
  juneminfee,
  permitorlicenseenddate,
  augustminfee,
  origcontracexpdate, operatorstatus, februaryminfee
FROM ranked_data
WHERE row_num <= 10

detailed_results.query: Can you show me, for each active operator whose operator status is set to 1, their person ID and operator last name from the park concession contracts, along with the corresponding person ID and operator last name from the related fee and contract info records? I'd like the results grouped into fee categories based on the permit or license fee, with a count of how many entries fall into each category, plus the average, total, and highest permit or license fee within each group. Please base this only on those records where the park concession contracts are linked through the matching contract code and location details, and include the categorized fee information along with the February minimum fee for grouping purposes, but not the specific June and August minimum fees in the final output.
detailed_results.sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t1.personid,
    t1.operatorlastname,
    t3.personid AS t3_personid,
    t4.operatorlastname AS t4_operatorlastname,
    t3.permitorlicensefee,
    t4.juneminfee,
    t5.augustminfee,
    CASE 
      WHEN t3.permitorlicensefee > 500 THEN 'high_fee'
      WHEN t3.permitorlicensefee > 200 THEN 'medium_fee'
      ELSE 'low_fee'
    END AS category, t2.februaryminfee
  FROM `Parks Concessions_park_concession_contracts` t1
  INNER JOIN `node_2` t2 ON t1.contractcode = t2.contractcode
  INNER JOIN `Parks Concessions_park_concession_fees` t3 ON t1.personid = t3.personid
  INNER JOIN `Parks Concessions_concession_contracts_info` t4 ON t1.operatorlastname = t4.operatorlastname
  INNER JOIN `Parks Concessions_concession_contracts_details` t5 ON t2.addlocationinfo1 = t5.addlocationinfo1
  WHERE t1.operatorstatus = 1.0
)
SELECT 
  personid,
  operatorlastname,
  t3_personid,
  t4_operatorlastname,
  category,
  COUNT(*) AS count,
  AVG(permitorlicensefee) AS avg_value,
  SUM(permitorlicensefee) AS total_value,
  MAX(permitorlicensefee) AS max_value
FROM categorized_data
GROUP BY 
  personid,
  operatorlastname,
  t3_personid,
  t4_operatorlastname,
  category, februaryminfee

detailed_results.sql:
WITH ranked_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t3.seg_ind,
    t3.empcity,
    t3.intempst,
    t3.intcity,
    t5.candfirst,
    t5.schedule,
    t5.matchamnt,
    t5.pay_method,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t3.intempst ORDER BY t5.matchamnt DESC) AS row_num, t1.rr_ind, t2.int_c_code, t4.boroughcd
  FROM `Doing Business Contributions Summary_business_contributions_summary_1` t1
  INNER JOIN `Doing Business Contributions Summary_business_contributions_summary` t2 ON t1.refno = t2.refno
  INNER JOIN `Doing Business Contributions Summary_business_contributors_locations` t3 ON t1.name = t3.name
  INNER JOIN `Doing Business Contributions Summary_political_contributions_summary` t4 ON t2.empname = t4.empname
  INNER JOIN `Doing Business Contributions Summary_business_contributions_summary_2` t5 ON t4.db_entity_name = t5.db_entity_name
  WHERE t5.schedule = 'ABC'
)
SELECT 
  seg_ind,
  empcity,
  intempst,
  intcity,
  candfirst,
  schedule,
  matchamnt,
  pay_method, rr_ind, int_c_code, boroughcd
FROM ranked_data
WHERE row_num <= 5

detailed_results.query: Can you give me a breakdown of each contributor using the contributor's `name` from the business contributions summary, along with the `name` of the associated location and its `seg_ind` from the business contributors locations data, and show which `candid` they supported, the `schedule` their contribution was reported under, and the contribution `category` based on the `matchamnt`? For each unique combination of contributor `name`, location `name`, `candid`, `seg_ind`, `schedule`, `category`, `int_c_code`, and `boroughcd`, please summarize the matched contribution amounts by returning the count of records, the average `matchamnt`, the total `matchamnt`, and the maximum `matchamnt`, but only include rows where `matchamnt` is not null.
detailed_results.sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t1.name AS contributor_name,
    t3.name AS location_name,
    t1.candid,
    t3.seg_ind,
    t5.schedule,
    t5.matchamnt,
    CASE 
      WHEN t5.matchamnt > 10000 THEN 'high'
      WHEN t5.matchamnt > 1000 THEN 'medium'
      ELSE 'low'
    END AS category, t2.int_c_code, t4.boroughcd
  FROM `Doing Business Contributions Summary_business_contributions_summary_1` t1
  INNER JOIN `Doing Business Contributions Summary_business_contributions_summary` t2 ON t1.refno = t2.refno
  INNER JOIN `Doing Business Contributions Summary_business_contributors_locations` t3 ON t1.name = t3.name
  INNER JOIN `Doing Business Contributions Summary_political_contributions_summary` t4 ON t2.empname = t4.empname
  INNER JOIN `Doing Business Contributions Summary_business_contributions_summary_2` t5 ON t4.db_entity_name = t5.db_entity_name
  WHERE t5.matchamnt IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
  contributor_name,
  location_name,
  candid,
  seg_ind,
  schedule,
  category,
  COUNT(*) AS count,
  AVG(matchamnt) AS avg_value,
  SUM(matchamnt) AS total_value,
  MAX(matchamnt) AS max_value
FROM categorized_data
GROUP BY 
  contributor_name,
  location_name,
  candid,
  seg_ind,
  schedule,
  category, int_c_code, boroughcd

detailed_results.query: Can you show me, for each business or organization, the top five contributions by amount, including the segment or category they fall into, the contributor's city, how much was given, which committee received it, the reporting schedule it was filed under, the first name of the candidate associated with each contribution, along with the rank of each contribution, the dense rank based on schedule and amount, the rr indicator, and the international contributor code?
detailed_results.sql:
WITH ranked AS (
  SELECT 
    t3.seg_ind,
    t3.intcity,
    t4.db_entity_name,
    t4.amnt,
    t4.committee,
    t5.db_entity_name,
    t5.schedule,
    t5.candfirst,
    RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY t4.db_entity_name ORDER BY t4.amnt DESC) AS rank,
    DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY t5.schedule ORDER BY t4.amnt) AS dense_rank, t1.rr_ind, t2.int_c_code
  FROM `Doing Business Contributions Summary_business_contributions_summary_1` t1
  INNER JOIN `Doing Business Contributions Summary_business_contributions_summary` t2 ON t1.refno = t2.refno
  INNER JOIN `Doing Business Contributions Summary_business_contributors_locations` t3 ON t1.name = t3.name
  INNER JOIN `Doing Business Contributions Summary_political_contributions_summary` t4 ON t2.empname = t4.empname
  INNER JOIN `Doing Business Contributions Summary_business_contributions_summary_2` t5 ON t4.db_entity_name = t5.db_entity_name
)
SELECT 
  seg_ind,
  intcity,
  db_entity_name,
  amnt,
  committee,
  schedule,
  candfirst,
  rank,
  dense_rank, rr_ind, int_c_code
FROM ranked
WHERE rank <= 5

  SELECT 
    t1.name AS contributor_name,

)
SELECT 
  contributor_name,
  location_name,
  db_entity_name,
  recipient_entity_name,
  amnt,
  intcity,
  schedule, int_c_code
FROM ranked_data
WHERE row_num <= 5

detailed_results.query: In the Doing Business Contributions Summary data, can you show me, for each db_entity_name, which empname is listed, which contributor_empname actually made the contribution, which filing_entity_name it is associated with, the seg_ind value for that record, the rr_ind value, and the schedule it is reported under? I'd like this summarized by contribution category based on amnt (small, medium, or large), including the count of records, the average amnt, the total amnt, and the maximum amnt for each combination of db_entity_name, empname, contributor_empname, filing_entity_name, seg_ind, schedule, category, and rr_ind.
detailed_results.sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t4.db_entity_name,
    t4.empname,
    t2.empname AS contributor_empname,
    t5.db_entity_name AS filing_entity_name,
    t3.seg_ind,
    t4.amnt,
    t5.schedule,
    CASE 
      WHEN t4.amnt > 1000 THEN 'large'
      WHEN t4.amnt > 100 THEN 'medium'
      ELSE 'small'
    END as category, t1.rr_ind
  FROM `Doing Business Contributions Summary_business_contributions_summary_1` t1
  INNER JOIN `Doing Business Contributions Summary_business_contributions_summary` t2 ON t1.refno = t2.refno
  INNER JOIN `Doing Business Contributions Summary_business_contributors_locations` t3 ON t1.name = t3.name
  INNER JOIN `Doing Business Contributions Summary_political_contributions_summary` t4 ON t2.empname = t4.empname
  INNER JOIN `Doing Business Contributions Summary_business_contributions_summary_2` t5 ON t4.db_entity_name = t5.db_entity_name
  WHERE t4.amnt IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
  db_entity_name,
  empname,
  contributor_empname,
  filing_entity_name,
  seg_ind,
  schedule,
  category,
  COUNT(*) as count,
  AVG(amnt) as avg_value,
  SUM(amnt) as total_value,
  MAX(amnt) as max_value
FROM categorized_data
GROUP BY 
  db_entity_name,
  empname,
  contributor_empname,
  filing_entity_name,
  seg_ind,
  schedule,
  category, rr_ind

detailed_results.query: Can you pull a list of the top business or organizational entities with positive total contribution amounts under schedule ABC, showing for each one the contributor’s name, the related employee’s name, the city they’re associated with, and the total, average, and number of contributions, ordered from the largest total amount down and limited to about the first hundred records?
detailed_results.sql:
WITH base_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t1.refno,
    t1.name AS contributor_name,
    t2.empname,
    t2.refno AS t2_refno,
    t3.name AS t3_name,
    t3.intcity,
    t4.empname AS t4_empname,
    t4.db_entity_name AS t4_db_entity_name,
    t4.amnt,
    t5.db_entity_name,
    t5.schedule
  FROM `Doing Business Contributions Summary_business_contributions_summary_1` t1
  INNER JOIN `Doing Business Contributions Summary_business_contributions_summary` t2 ON t1.refno = t2.refno
  INNER JOIN `Doing Business Contributions Summary_business_contributors_locations` t3 ON t1.name = t3.name
  INNER JOIN `Doing Business Contributions Summary_political_contributions_summary` t4 ON t2.empname = t4.empname
  INNER JOIN `Doing Business Contributions Summary_business_contributions_summary_2` t5 ON t4.db_entity_name = t5.db_entity_name
  WHERE t5.schedule = 'ABC'
),
aggregated AS (
  SELECT 
    db_entity_name,
    contributor_name,
    empname,
    intcity,
    schedule,
    SUM(amnt) AS total,
    COUNT(*) AS count,
    AVG(amnt) AS average
  FROM base_data
  GROUP BY db_entity_name, contributor_name, empname, intcity, schedule
)
SELECT 
  db_entity_name,
  contributor_name,
  empname,
  intcity,
  schedule,
  total,
  count,
  average
FROM aggregated
WHERE total > 0
ORDER BY total DESC
LIMIT 100

detailed_results.sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t1.ppt_id,
    t1.latitude,
    t1.longitude,
    t1.site_id,
    t1.address,
    t2.site_id AS t2_site_id,
    t3.ppt_id AS t3_ppt_id,
    t4.latitude AS t4_latitude,
    t4.longitude AS t4_longitude,
    t5.address AS t5_address,
    t2.phone_status_date,
    t3.phone_status,
    t4.tablet_status,
    t5.wifi_status_date,
    CASE 
      WHEN t4.install_date > '2025-01-01' THEN 'new'
      WHEN t4.install_date > '2020-01-01' THEN 'medium'
      ELSE 'old'
    END AS category
  FROM `LinkNYC Kiosk Status_linknyc_kiosk_locations_1` t1
  INNER JOIN `LinkNYC Kiosk Status_linknyc_kiosk_statuses` t2 ON t1.site_id = t2.site_id
  INNER JOIN `LinkNYC Kiosk Status_linknyc_kiosk_status` t3 ON t1.ppt_id = t3.ppt_id
  INNER JOIN `LinkNYC Kiosk Status_linknyc_kiosk_locations` t4 ON t1.latitude = t4.latitude AND t1.longitude = t4.longitude
  INNER JOIN `LinkNYC Kiosk Status_linknyc_kiosk_status_1` t5 ON t1.address = t5.address
  WHERE t4.install_date IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
  ppt_id,
  address,
  phone_status,
  tablet_status,
  category,
  COUNT(*) AS count,
  AVG(0) AS avg_value,
  SUM(0) AS total_value,
  MAX(0) AS max_value
FROM categorized_data
GROUP BY 
  ppt_id,
  address,
  phone_status,
  tablet_status,
  category

detailed_results.query: Can you show me, for each high school, how many program entries it has in each college‑ and career‑readiness category (High, Medium, or Low based on college_career_rate thresholds of 80% and 50%), along with the school's name, borough, the average college and career readiness rate, the total college and career readiness rate, and the maximum college and career readiness rate across those programs?
detailed_results.sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t3.school_name,
    t3.attendance_rate,
    t4.pct_stu_safe,
    t5.boro,
    t6.college_career_rate,
    t6.seats3specialized,
    CASE 
      WHEN t6.college_career_rate > 80 THEN 'High College/Career Readiness'
      WHEN t6.college_career_rate > 50 THEN 'Medium College/Career Readiness'
      ELSE 'Low College/Career Readiness'
    END as category, t1.prgdesc1, t2.grade9geapplicantsperseat1
  FROM `2018 DOE High School Directory_high_school_directory_2018` t1
  INNER JOIN `2018 DOE High School Directory_high_school_programs` t2 ON t1.dbn = t2.dbn
  INNER JOIN `node_3` t3 ON t1.school_name = t3.school_name
  INNER JOIN `2018 DOE High School Directory_high_school_programs_info` t4 ON t1.fax_number = t4.fax_number
  INNER JOIN `2018 DOE High School Directory_high_school_programs_info_2` t5 ON t2.phone_number = t5.phone_number
  INNER JOIN `2018 DOE High School Directory_high_school_programs_info_1` t6 ON t2.code1 = t6.code1
  WHERE t3.attendance_rate IS NOT NULL AND t6.college_career_rate IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
  school_name,
  boro,
  category,
  COUNT(*) as count,
  AVG(college_career_rate) as avg_value,
  SUM(college_career_rate) as total_value,
  MAX(college_career_rate) as max_value
FROM categorized_data
GROUP BY school_name, boro, category, prgdesc1, grade9geapplicantsperseat1

detailed_results.query: Show about 20 high schools from the 2018 DOE High School Directory with the highest average college and career readiness rate, including each school's name from both t1 and t3 tables, fax number from both t1 and t4 tables, borough, the total average college and career readiness rate, count of records, the average rate, and grade 9 GE applicants per seat, ranked from highest to lowest on that readiness rate.
detailed_results.sql:
WITH base_data AS (
SELECT t1.school_name AS t1_school_name,
       t1.fax_number AS t1_fax_number,
       t3.school_name AS t3_school_name,
       t4.fax_number AS t4_fax_number,
       t3.attendance_rate,
       t4.pct_stu_safe,
       t5.boro,
       t6.college_career_rate, t2.grade9geapplicantsperseat1
FROM `2018 DOE High School Directory_high_school_directory_2018` t1
INNER JOIN `2018 DOE High School Directory_high_school_programs` t2 ON t1.dbn = t2.dbn
INNER JOIN `node_3` t3 ON t1.school_name = t3.school_name
INNER JOIN `2018 DOE High School Directory_high_school_programs_info` t4 ON t1.fax_number = t4.fax_number
INNER JOIN `2018 DOE High School Directory_high_school_programs_info_2` t5 ON t2.phone_number = t5.phone_number
INNER JOIN `2018 DOE High School Directory_high_school_programs_info_1` t6 ON t2.code1 = t6.code1
WHERE t3.attendance_rate IS NOT NULL
  AND t6.college_career_rate IS NOT NULL
),
aggregated AS (
SELECT t1_school_name,
       t1_fax_number,
       t3_school_name,
       t4_fax_number,
       boro,
       AVG(college_career_rate) AS total,
       COUNT(*) AS count,
       AVG(college_career_rate) AS average
FROM base_data
GROUP BY t1_school_name,
         t1_fax_number,
         t3_school_name,
         t4_fax_number,
         boro, grade9geapplicantsperseat1
)
SELECT t1_school_name,
       t1_fax_number,
       t3_school_name,
       t4_fax_number,
       boro,
       total,
       count,
       average, grade9geapplicantsperseat1
FROM aggregated
WHERE total > 0
ORDER BY total DESC
LIMIT 20

INNER JOIN `2019 - 2020 School Locations_school_location_details` t3 ON t1.location_code = t3.location_code
INNER JOIN `2019 - 2020 School Locations_school_location_details_1` t4 ON t1.location_name = t4.location_name
INNER JOIN `2019 - 2020 School Locations_school_location_details_3` t5 ON t2.beds = t5.beds WHERE t3.fiscal_year IS NOT NULL) SELECT location_name, location_code, t3_location_code, t4_location_name, category, COUNT(*) as count, AVG(fiscal_year) as avg_value, SUM(fiscal_year) as total_value, MAX(fiscal_year) as max_value FROM categorized_data GROUP BY location_name, location_code, t3_location_code, t4_location_name, category, highschool_network_location

detailed_results.sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (SELECT t1.work_permit, t1.job_filing_number, t3.work_permit AS t3_work_permit, t4.job_filing_number AS t4_job_filing_number, t3.issued_date, t4.estimated_job_costs, t5.permit_status, CASE WHEN t4.estimated_job_costs > 500000 THEN 'High Cost' WHEN t4.estimated_job_costs > 50000 THEN 'Medium Cost' ELSE 'Low Cost' END as category, t2.approved_date FROM `DOB NOW： Build – Approved Permits_approved_building_permits_2` t1
INNER JOIN `DOB NOW： Build – Approved Permits_approved_building_permits` t2 ON t1.tracking_number = t2.tracking_number
INNER JOIN `DOB NOW： Build – Approved Permits_approved_building_permits_4` t3 ON t1.work_permit = t3.work_permit
INNER JOIN `DOB NOW： Build – Approved Permits_approved_building_permits_3` t4 ON t1.job_filing_number = t4.job_filing_number
INNER JOIN `DOB NOW： Build – Approved Permits_approved_building_permits_1` t5 ON t2.bin = t5.bin WHERE t5.permit_status IS NOT NULL) SELECT job_filing_number, work_permit, permit_status, category, COUNT(*) as count, AVG(estimated_job_costs) as avg_value, SUM(estimated_job_costs) as total_value, MAX(estimated_job_costs) as max_value FROM categorized_data GROUP BY job_filing_number, work_permit, permit_status, category, approved_date

detailed_results.query: Could you show me, for each property block and its listed owner, along with the block from tax assessment, owner from valuation records, exemption code, exempt land amount, and assessed land value, how many related records there are, along with the average, total, and highest overall assessed value, and also break that out by value categories (High Value for over 1 million, Medium Value for over 500k, and Low Value for the rest) and valuation type, grouped so I can see these numbers per block-owner-exemption-land combination and how they fall into the different value categories?
detailed_results.sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (SELECT t1.block, t1.owner, t3.block, t4.owner, t1.avtot, t3.excd1, t4.exland2, t5.avland, CASE WHEN t1.avtot > 1000000 THEN 'High Value' WHEN t1.avtot > 500000 THEN 'Medium Value' ELSE 'Low Value' END as category, t2.valtype FROM `Property Valuation and Assessment Data_property_valuation_records` t1
INNER JOIN `Property Valuation and Assessment Data_property_assessment_records` t2 ON t1.bble = t2.bble
INNER JOIN `Property Valuation and Assessment Data_property_tax_assessment` t3 ON t1.block = t3.block
INNER JOIN `Property Valuation and Assessment Data_property_valuation_records_1` t4 ON t1.owner = t4.owner
INNER JOIN `Property Valuation and Assessment Data_property_valuation_records_2` t5 ON t2.staddr = t5.staddr WHERE t1.avtot IS NOT NULL) SELECT block, owner, excd1, exland2, avland, category, COUNT(*) as count, AVG(avtot) as avg_value, SUM(avtot) as total_value, MAX(avtot) as max_value FROM categorized_data GROUP BY block, owner, excd1, exland2, avland, category, valtype

detailed_results.query: Could you pull a summary of properties where the same person owns at least five places on the same city block, showing for each of those owners the street address and block, along with any exemption category tied to the block, the assessed land value, and the total, average, highest, and lowest tax or expense amount recorded for those properties?
detailed_results.sql:
WITH base_data AS (SELECT t1.owner, t1.block, t1.bble, t2.bble AS t2_bble, t2.staddr, t3.block AS t3_block, t4.owner AS t4_owner, t3.excd1, t4.avland2, t5.extot FROM `Property Valuation and Assessment Data_property_valuation_records` t1
INNER JOIN `Property Valuation and Assessment Data_property_assessment_records` t2 ON t1.bble = t2.bble
INNER JOIN `Property Valuation and Assessment Data_property_tax_assessment` t3 ON t1.block = t3.block
INNER JOIN `Property Valuation and Assessment Data_property_valuation_records_1` t4 ON t1.owner = t4.owner
INNER JOIN `Property Valuation and Assessment Data_property_valuation_records_2` t5 ON t2.staddr = t5.staddr WHERE t1.avtot IS NOT NULL) SELECT owner, staddr, block, AVG(extot) as record_count, SUM(extot) as total_amount, AVG(extot) as avg_amount, MAX(extot) as max_amount, MIN(extot) as min_amount FROM base_data GROUP BY owner, staddr, block HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5

detailed_results.sql:
WITH ranked_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t3.queens_condominium_property_neighborhood,
    t3.queens_condominium_property_market_value_per_sqft,
    t5.queens_condominium_property_full_market_value,
    t5.queens_condominium_property_est_gross_income,
    t5.queens_condominium_property_gross_income_per_sqft,
    t5.latitude,
    t5.longitude,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY t3.queens_condominium_property_neighborhood 
      ORDER BY t5.queens_condominium_property_gross_income_per_sqft DESC
    ) AS row_num, t1.comparable_rental_2_total_units, t2.comparable_rental_2_gross_sqft, t4.longitude
  FROM `DOF： Condominium comparable rental income – Queens - FY 2010 2011_queens_condo_rental_income` t1
  INNER JOIN `DOF： Condominium comparable rental income – Queens - FY 2010 2011_queens_condo_rental_income_2010_2011` t2 
    ON t1.queens_condominium_property_condo_section = t2.queens_condominium_property_condo_section
  INNER JOIN `DOF： Condominium comparable rental income – Queens - FY 2010 2011_queens_condo_rental_comparisons` t3 
    ON t1.queens_condominium_property_address = t3.queens_condominium_property_address
  INNER JOIN `DOF： Condominium comparable rental income – Queens - FY 2010 2011_queens_condo_rental_comparables` t4 
    ON t2.queens_condominium_property_boro_block_lot = t4.queens_condominium_property_boro_block_lot
  INNER JOIN `node_5` t5 
    ON t4.latitude = t5.latitude AND t4.longitude = t5.longitude 
  WHERE t5.queens_condominium_property_est_gross_income IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
  queens_condominium_property_neighborhood,
  queens_condominium_property_market_value_per_sqft,
  queens_condominium_property_full_market_value,
  queens_condominium_property_est_gross_income,
  queens_condominium_property_gross_income_per_sqft,
  latitude,
  longitude, comparable_rental_2_total_units, comparable_rental_2_gross_sqft, longitude
FROM ranked_data
WHERE row_num <= 3

detailed_results.sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (SELECT t1.queens_condominium_property_address, t3.queens_condominium_property_address, t1.queens_condominium_property_condo_section, t3.queens_condominium_property_neighborhood, t3.queens_condominium_property_market_value_per_sqft, t5.queens_condominium_property_est_gross_income, CASE WHEN t5.queens_condominium_property_est_gross_income > 4000000 THEN 'high income' WHEN t5.queens_condominium_property_est_gross_income > 2000000 THEN 'medium income' ELSE 'low income' END as category, t2.comparable_rental_2_gross_sqft, t4.longitude FROM `DOF： Condominium comparable rental income – Queens - FY 2010 2011_queens_condo_rental_income` t1
INNER JOIN `DOF： Condominium comparable rental income – Queens - FY 2010 2011_queens_condo_rental_income_2010_2011` t2 ON t1.queens_condominium_property_condo_section = t2.queens_condominium_property_condo_section
INNER JOIN `DOF： Condominium comparable rental income – Queens - FY 2010 2011_queens_condo_rental_comparisons` t3 ON t1.queens_condominium_property_address = t3.queens_condominium_property_address
INNER JOIN `DOF： Condominium comparable rental income – Queens - FY 2010 2011_queens_condo_rental_comparables` t4 ON t2.queens_condominium_property_boro_block_lot = t4.queens_condominium_property_boro_block_lot
INNER JOIN `node_5` t5 ON t4.latitude = t5.latitude AND t4.longitude = t5.longitude WHERE t5.queens_condominium_property_est_gross_income IS NOT NULL) SELECT queens_condominium_property_neighborhood, category, COUNT(*) as count, AVG(queens_condominium_property_est_gross_income) as avg_value, SUM(queens_condominium_property_est_gross_income) as total_value, MAX(queens_condominium_property_est_gross_income) as max_value FROM categorized_data GROUP BY queens_condominium_property_neighborhood, category, comparable_rental_2_gross_sqft, longitude

detailed_results.query: Can you show me, for each neighborhood in Queens, a breakdown of the different condo sections and their specific street addresses, along with how many records you have for each address (grouped by longitude as well) and the total, average, highest, and lowest estimated gross rental income associated with them, but only include addresses with at least 1 record?
detailed_results.sql:
WITH base_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t1.queens_condominium_property_condo_section,
    t1.queens_condominium_property_address,
    t2.queens_condominium_property_condo_section,
    t3.queens_condominium_property_address,
    t3.queens_condominium_property_neighborhood,
    t5.queens_condominium_property_est_gross_income, t4.longitude
  FROM `DOF： Condominium comparable rental income – Queens - FY 2010 2011_queens_condo_rental_income` t1
  INNER JOIN `DOF： Condominium comparable rental income – Queens - FY 2010 2011_queens_condo_rental_income_2010_2011` t2 ON t1.queens_condominium_property_condo_section = t2.queens_condominium_property_condo_section
  INNER JOIN `DOF： Condominium comparable rental income – Queens - FY 2010 2011_queens_condo_rental_comparisons` t3 ON t1.queens_condominium_property_address = t3.queens_condominium_property_address
  INNER JOIN `DOF： Condominium comparable rental income – Queens - FY 2010 2011_queens_condo_rental_comparables` t4 ON t2.queens_condominium_property_boro_block_lot = t4.queens_condominium_property_boro_block_lot
  INNER JOIN `node_5` t5 ON t4.latitude = t5.latitude AND t4.longitude = t5.longitude
  WHERE t5.queens_condominium_property_est_gross_income IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
  queens_condominium_property_neighborhood,
  queens_condominium_property_condo_section,
  queens_condominium_property_address,
  COUNT(*) AS record_count,
  SUM(queens_condominium_property_est_gross_income) AS total_amount,
  AVG(queens_condominium_property_est_gross_income) AS avg_amount,
  MAX(queens_condominium_property_est_gross_income) AS max_amount,
  MIN(queens_condominium_property_est_gross_income) AS min_amount
FROM base_data
GROUP BY 
  queens_condominium_property_neighborhood,
  queens_condominium_property_condo_section,
  queens_condominium_property_address, longitude
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 1

WITH ranked_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t1.queens_condominium_property_address,
    t3.queens_condominium_property_address AS t3_queens_condominium_property_address,
    t3.queens_condominium_property_neighborhood,
    t3.queens_condominium_property_market_value_per_sqft,
    t4.latitude,
    t4.longitude,
    t4.queens_condominium_property_year_built,
    t5.latitude AS t5_latitude,
    t5.longitude AS t5_longitude,
    t5.queens_condominium_property_est_gross_income,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY t3.queens_condominium_property_neighborhood 
      ORDER BY t5.queens_condominium_property_est_gross_income DESC
    ) AS row_num, t2.comparable_rental_2_gross_sqft
  FROM `DOF： Condominium comparable rental income – Queens - FY 2010 2011_queens_condo_rental_income` t1
  INNER JOIN `DOF： Condominium comparable rental income – Queens - FY 2010 2011_queens_condo_rental_income_2010_2011` t2 
    ON t1.queens_condominium_property_condo_section = t2.queens_condominium_property_condo_section
  INNER JOIN `DOF： Condominium comparable rental income – Queens - FY 2010 2011_queens_condo_rental_comparisons` t3 
    ON t1.queens_condominium_property_address = t3.queens_condominium_property_address
  INNER JOIN `DOF： Condominium comparable rental income – Queens - FY 2010 2011_queens_condo_rental_comparables` t4 
    ON t2.queens_condominium_property_boro_block_lot = t4.queens_condominium_property_boro_block_lot
  INNER JOIN `node_5` t5 
    ON t4.latitude = t5.latitude AND t4.longitude = t5.longitude
  WHERE t3.queens_condominium_property_market_value_per_sqft IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
  queens_condominium_property_address,
  t3_queens_condominium_property_address,
  queens_condominium_property_neighborhood,
  queens_condominium_property_market_value_per_sqft,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  t5_latitude,
  t5_longitude,
  queens_condominium_property_est_gross_income, comparable_rental_2_gross_sqft
FROM ranked_data
WHERE row_num <= 3

detailed_results.sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t2.queens_condominium_property_boro_block_lot,
    t3.queens_condominium_property_neighborhood,
    t4.queens_condominium_property_boro_block_lot AS t4_queens_condominium_property_boro_block_lot,
    t4.latitude,
    t4.longitude,
    t5.latitude AS t5_latitude,
    t5.longitude AS t5_longitude,
    t5.queens_condominium_property_full_market_value,
    CASE 
      WHEN t5.queens_condominium_property_full_market_value > 10000000 THEN 'High value'
      WHEN t5.queens_condominium_property_full_market_value > 5000000 THEN 'Medium value'
      ELSE 'Low value'
    END AS category, t1.comparable_rental_2_total_units
  FROM `DOF： Condominium comparable rental income – Queens - FY 2010 2011_queens_condo_rental_income` t1
  INNER JOIN `DOF： Condominium comparable rental income – Queens - FY 2010 2011_queens_condo_rental_income_2010_2011` t2 
    ON t1.queens_condominium_property_condo_section = t2.queens_condominium_property_condo_section
  INNER JOIN `DOF： Condominium comparable rental income – Queens - FY 2010 2011_queens_condo_rental_comparisons` t3 
    ON t1.queens_condominium_property_address = t3.queens_condominium_property_address
  INNER JOIN `DOF： Condominium comparable rental income – Queens - FY 2010 2011_queens_condo_rental_comparables` t4 
    ON t2.queens_condominium_property_boro_block_lot = t4.queens_condominium_property_boro_block_lot
  INNER JOIN `node_5` t5 
    ON t4.latitude = t5.latitude AND t4.longitude = t5.longitude
  WHERE t5.queens_condominium_property_full_market_value IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
  queens_condominium_property_neighborhood,
  category,
  COUNT(*) AS count,
  AVG(queens_condominium_property_full_market_value) AS avg_value,
  SUM(queens_condominium_property_full_market_value) AS total_value,
  MAX(queens_condominium_property_full_market_value) AS max_value
FROM categorized_data
GROUP BY 
  queens_condominium_property_neighborhood,
  category, comparable_rental_2_total_units

detailed_results.query: Could you show me, for each type of childcare program, kind of facility, inspection summary result, and permit number, how many centers fall into each risk category, along with the average, total, and highest average public health hazard violation rates, based on each center's name and most recent inspection date?
detailed_results.sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t3.programtype,
    t3.publichealthhazardviolationrate,
    t4.centername,
    t4.inspectiondate,
    t5.facilitytype,
    t6.averagepublichealthhazardiolationrate,
    CASE 
      WHEN t6.averagepublichealthhazardiolationrate > 10 THEN 'High Risk'
      WHEN t6.averagepublichealthhazardiolationrate > 5 THEN 'Medium Risk'
      ELSE 'Low Risk'
    END AS category, t1.inspectionsummaryresult, t2.permitnumber
  FROM `DOHMH Childcare Center Inspections_childcare_center_inspections` t1
  INNER JOIN `DOHMH Childcare Center Inspections_childcare_inspection_records` t2 ON t1.dc_id = t2.dc_id
  INNER JOIN `node_3` t3 ON t1.phone = t3.phone
  INNER JOIN `DOHMH Childcare Center Inspections_childcare_inspection_records_1` t4 ON t1.centername = t4.centername
  INNER JOIN `DOHMH Childcare Center Inspections_childcare_center_inspections_1` t5 ON t2.legalname = t5.legalname
  INNER JOIN `DOHMH Childcare Center Inspections_childcare_inspection_results` t6 ON t2.bin = t6.bin
  WHERE t4.inspectiondate IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
  programtype,
  facilitytype,
  category,
  COUNT(*) AS count,
  AVG(averagepublichealthhazardiolationrate) AS avg_value,
  SUM(averagepublichealthhazardiolationrate) AS total_value,
  MAX(averagepublichealthhazardiolationrate) AS max_value
FROM categorized_data
GROUP BY 
  programtype,
  facilitytype,
  category, inspectionsummaryresult, permitnumber

detailed_results.query: Can you pull a list of the top 100 child care centers (ranked by their total violation rate since 2020) and show, for each one, the center's name, a contact phone number, the overall outcome of their most recent inspection, the type of program they run, the center name from violation records, the total violation rate, the count of violations, the average violation rate, and the permit number?
detailed_results.sql:
WITH base_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t1.centername,
    t1.phone,
    t1.inspectionsummaryresult,
    t3.phone AS t3_phone,
    t3.programtype,
    t4.centername AS t4_centername,
    t4.violationratepercent,
    t5.totaleducationalworkers,
    t6.averagepublichealthhazardiolationrate, t2.permitnumber
  FROM `DOHMH Childcare Center Inspections_childcare_center_inspections` t1
  INNER JOIN `DOHMH Childcare Center Inspections_childcare_inspection_records` t2 ON t1.dc_id = t2.dc_id
  INNER JOIN `node_3` t3 ON t1.phone = t3.phone
  INNER JOIN `DOHMH Childcare Center Inspections_childcare_inspection_records_1` t4 ON t1.centername = t4.centername
  INNER JOIN `DOHMH Childcare Center Inspections_childcare_center_inspections_1` t5 ON t2.legalname = t5.legalname
  INNER JOIN `DOHMH Childcare Center Inspections_childcare_inspection_results` t6 ON t2.bin = t6.bin 
  WHERE t4.inspectiondate >= '2020-01-01'
),
aggregated AS (
  SELECT 
    centername,
    phone,
    inspectionsummaryresult,
    programtype,
    t4_centername,
    SUM(violationratepercent) AS total,
    COUNT(*) AS count,
    AVG(violationratepercent) AS average
  FROM base_data
  GROUP BY centername, phone, inspectionsummaryresult, programtype, t4_centername, permitnumber
)
SELECT 
  centername,
  phone,
  inspectionsummaryresult,
  programtype,
  t4_centername,
  total,
  count,
  average, permitnumber
FROM aggregated
WHERE average > 0
ORDER BY total DESC
LIMIT 100

detailed_results.query: Can you show me, for each unique building/location (bin), provider name (legalname), what kind of childcare they run (childcaretype), the specific program category they fall under (programtype), the type of facility it is (facilitytype), the additional provider name from the center inspections table (t5_legalname), the building identifier from the inspection results (t6_bin), the inspection dates since the start of 2020, and the inspection summary result, along with how many inspection records there are for each of those combinations (only where there are at least five records), and the total, average, highest, and lowest average public health hazard violation rate for each of those?
detailed_results.sql:
WITH base_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t2.bin,
    t2.legalname,
    t2.childcaretype,
    t3.programtype,
    t4.inspectiondate,
    t5.legalname AS t5_legalname,
    t5.facilitytype,
    t6.bin AS t6_bin,
    t6.averagepublichealthhazardiolationrate, t1.inspectionsummaryresult
  FROM `DOHMH Childcare Center Inspections_childcare_center_inspections` t1
  INNER JOIN `DOHMH Childcare Center Inspections_childcare_inspection_records` t2 ON t1.dc_id = t2.dc_id
  INNER JOIN `node_3` t3 ON t1.phone = t3.phone
  INNER JOIN `DOHMH Childcare Center Inspections_childcare_inspection_records_1` t4 ON t1.centername = t4.centername
  INNER JOIN `DOHMH Childcare Center Inspections_childcare_center_inspections_1` t5 ON t2.legalname = t5.legalname
  INNER JOIN `DOHMH Childcare Center Inspections_childcare_inspection_results` t6 ON t2.bin = t6.bin
  WHERE t4.inspectiondate >= '2020-01-01'
)
SELECT 
  bin,
  legalname,
  childcaretype,
  programtype,
  facilitytype,
  t5_legalname,
  t6_bin,
  inspectiondate,
  COUNT(*) as record_count,
  SUM(averagepublichealthhazardiolationrate) as total_amount,
  AVG(averagepublichealthhazardiolationrate) as avg_amount,
  MAX(averagepublichealthhazardiolationrate) as max_amount,
  MIN(averagepublichealthhazardiolationrate) as min_amount
FROM base_data
GROUP BY 
  bin,
  legalname,
  childcaretype,
  programtype,
  facilitytype,
  t5_legalname,
  t6_bin,
  inspectiondate, inspectionsummaryresult
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5

detailed_results.query: For Staten Island, could you break down, by neighborhood council district, garbage pickup area, zip code, and longitude, how many street planting locations there are for each level of overhead utility lines (none, some, and high), along with the average, total, and highest amount of overhead lines in each group, and also include the borough name for those locations?
detailed_results.sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t3.buildingnumber,
    t3.overheadutilities,
    t4.width,
    t5.citycouncil,
    t5.boroughcode,
    t6.congressional,
    t6.sanitationzone,
    CASE 
      WHEN t3.overheadutilities > 5 THEN 'high overhead utilities'
      WHEN t3.overheadutilities > 0 THEN 'some overhead utilities'
      ELSE 'no overhead utilities'
    END as category, t1.zipcode, t2.longitude
  FROM `Forestry Planting Spaces_tree_planting_sites` t1
  INNER JOIN `node_2` t2 ON t1.objectid = t2.objectid
  INNER JOIN `Forestry Planting Spaces_street_tree_planting_locations` t3 ON t1.globalid = t3.globalid
  INNER JOIN `Forestry Planting Spaces_planting_space_locations` t4 ON t1.location = t4.location
  INNER JOIN `Forestry Planting Spaces_tree_planting_locations` t5 ON t2.bin = t5.bin
  INNER JOIN `Forestry Planting Spaces_street_tree_planting_sites` t6 ON t2.latitude = t6.latitude AND t2.longitude = t6.longitude
  WHERE t5.boroughcode = 'Staten Island'
)
SELECT 
  boroughcode,
  citycouncil,
  sanitationzone,
  category,
  COUNT(*) as count,
  AVG(overheadutilities) as avg_value,
  SUM(overheadutilities) as total_value,
  MAX(overheadutilities) as max_value
FROM categorized_data
GROUP BY 
  boroughcode,
  citycouncil,
  sanitationzone,
  category, zipcode, longitude

  SELECT 
    t3.nta2020,
    t3.residflag,
    t4.permityear,
    t4.zoningdst1,
    t4.floorsprop,
    t5.datelstupd,
    t5.job_status,
    t5.schelmntry,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY t3.nta2020 
      ORDER BY t4.permityear DESC
    ) AS row_num, t1.longitude, t2.occ_prop
  FROM `Housing Database Project Level Files_housing_project_details_1` t1
  INNER JOIN `Housing Database Project Level Files_housing_project_details` t2 
    ON t1.job_number = t2.job_number
  INNER JOIN `node_3` t3 
    ON t1.bin = t3.bin
  INNER JOIN `node_4` t4 
    ON t1.latitude = t4.latitude AND t1.longitude = t4.longitude
  INNER JOIN `Housing Database Project Level Files_housing_project_status` t5 
    ON t2.addressnum = t5.addressnum
  WHERE t4.permityear IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
  nta2020,
  residflag,
  permityear,
  zoningdst1,
  floorsprop,
  datelstupd,
  job_status,
  schelmntry, longitude, occ_prop
FROM ranked_data
WHERE row_num <= 5

WITH base_data AS (SELECT t2.addressnum, t2.ntaname20, t3.councildst, t4.permityear, t4.addressst, t5.addressnum as t5_addressnum, t5.schelmntry, t1.longitude FROM `Housing Database Project Level Files_housing_project_details_1` t1

detailed_results.query: For each lot in the Lot Cleaning Dispositions (No Longer Maintained) records, show only the single most recent inspection that has a non‑null lot status. Include the lot ID, whether the original settings were overridden, the lot entry date, the inspection request ID, the inspection detail entry date, the lot status ID, the lot status reason, the area, the lot billing total, and the coordinate y.
detailed_results.sql:
WITH ranked_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t3.lotid,
    t3.originaloverride,
    t3.lotentrydate,
    t5.inspectionrequestid,
    t5.detailentrydate,
    t5.lotstatusid,
    t5.lotstatusreason,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t3.lotid ORDER BY t5.detailentrydate DESC) AS row_num, t1.area, t2.lotbllingtotal, t4.coordinatey
  FROM `Lot Cleaning Dispositions (No Longer Maintained)_lot_cleaning_records_3` t1
  INNER JOIN `Lot Cleaning Dispositions (No Longer Maintained)_lot_cleaning_records_1` t2 ON t1.activitydetailid = t2.activitydetailid
  INNER JOIN `Lot Cleaning Dispositions (No Longer Maintained)_lot_cleaning_records` t3 ON t1.lotid = t3.lotid
  INNER JOIN `node_4` t4 ON t2.activityid = t4.activityid
  INNER JOIN `Lot Cleaning Dispositions (No Longer Maintained)_lot_cleaning_records_2` t5 ON t4.inspectionrequestid = t5.inspectionrequestid
  WHERE t5.lotstatusid IS NOT NULL
) 
SELECT 
  lotid,
  originaloverride,
  lotentrydate,
  inspectionrequestid,
  detailentrydate,
  lotstatusid,
  lotstatusreason, area, lotbllingtotal, coordinatey
FROM ranked_data
WHERE row_num <= 1

detailed_results.sql:
WITH ranked AS (
  SELECT 
    t5.inspectionrequestid,
    t4.inspectionrequestid,
    t3.originaloverride,
    t3.lotentrydate,
    t4.requeststatusid,
    t4.noofaddresses,
    t5.detailentrydate,
    t5.lotstatusid,
    RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY t5.inspectionrequestid ORDER BY t3.lotentrydate DESC) as rank,
    DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY t4.inspectionrequestid ORDER BY t4.requeststatusid) as dense_rank, t1.area, t2.lotbllingtotal
  FROM `Lot Cleaning Dispositions (No Longer Maintained)_lot_cleaning_records_3` t1
  INNER JOIN `Lot Cleaning Dispositions (No Longer Maintained)_lot_cleaning_records_1` t2 ON t1.activitydetailid = t2.activitydetailid
  INNER JOIN `Lot Cleaning Dispositions (No Longer Maintained)_lot_cleaning_records` t3 ON t1.lotid = t3.lotid
  INNER JOIN `node_4` t4 ON t2.activityid = t4.activityid
  INNER JOIN `Lot Cleaning Dispositions (No Longer Maintained)_lot_cleaning_records_2` t5 ON t4.inspectionrequestid = t5.inspectionrequestid
)
SELECT 
  inspectionrequestid,
  t4_inspectionrequestid,
  originaloverride,
  lotentrydate,
  requeststatusid,
  noofaddresses,
  detailentrydate,
  lotstatusid,
  rank,
  dense_rank
FROM (
  SELECT 
    inspectionrequestid,
    inspectionrequestid AS t5_inspectionrequestid,
    inspectionrequestid AS t4_inspectionrequestid,
    originaloverride,
    lotentrydate,
    requeststatusid,
    noofaddresses,
    detailentrydate,
    lotstatusid,
    rank,
    dense_rank, area, lotbllingtotal
  FROM ranked
) AS ranked_outer
WHERE rank <= 5

detailed_results.query: Could you show me a breakdown of each lot cleaning job in the Lot Cleaning Dispositions (No Longer Maintained) data where the total billing amount is not null, grouped by the various activity identifiers (including the t4 activity identifier), the related inspection request IDs (including both the main and t5 inspection request IDs), the area, and the original override recorded? For each group I want to see how many records there are, along with the average, total, and highest number of hours worked. Please also categorize each group of jobs as High Hours (more than 8 hours), Medium Hours (more than 4 hours), or Low Hours based on the number of hours from the inspection request records.
detailed_results.sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t2.activityid,
    t4.activityid AS t4_activityid,
    t4.inspectionrequestid,
    t5.inspectionrequestid AS t5_inspectionrequestid,
    t3.originaloverride,
    t5.hours,
    t2.lotbllingtotal,
    CASE 
      WHEN t5.hours > 8 THEN 'High Hours'
      WHEN t5.hours > 4 THEN 'Medium Hours'
      ELSE 'Low Hours'
    END AS category, t1.area
  FROM `Lot Cleaning Dispositions (No Longer Maintained)_lot_cleaning_records_3` t1
  INNER JOIN `Lot Cleaning Dispositions (No Longer Maintained)_lot_cleaning_records_1` t2 ON t1.activitydetailid = t2.activitydetailid
  INNER JOIN `Lot Cleaning Dispositions (No Longer Maintained)_lot_cleaning_records` t3 ON t1.lotid = t3.lotid
  INNER JOIN `node_4` t4 ON t2.activityid = t4.activityid
  INNER JOIN `Lot Cleaning Dispositions (No Longer Maintained)_lot_cleaning_records_2` t5 ON t4.inspectionrequestid = t5.inspectionrequestid
  WHERE t2.lotbllingtotal IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
  activityid,
  t4_activityid,
  inspectionrequestid,
  t5_inspectionrequestid,
  originaloverride,
  category,
  COUNT(*) AS count,
  AVG(hours) AS avg_value,
  SUM(hours) AS total_value,
  MAX(hours) AS max_value
FROM categorized_data
GROUP BY 
  activityid,
  t4_activityid,
  inspectionrequestid,
  t5_inspectionrequestid,
  originaloverride,
  category, area

detailed_results.sql:
WITH ranked_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t3.dbn,
    t3.programname,
    t3.geodistrict,
    t3.programtype,
    t3.accessibility,
    t5.address,
    t5.additionalpriorities,
    t5.extendedhoursallschools,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t3.geodistrict ORDER BY t5.additionalpriorities DESC) AS row_num, t1.geodistrict, t2.languagesupports, t4.languagesupportprograms
  FROM `2019 Pre-Kindergarten Admissions Guide_pre_k_admissions_data` t1
  INNER JOIN `2019 Pre-Kindergarten Admissions Guide_pre_k_admissions_manhattan` t2 ON t1.dbn = t2.dbn
  INNER JOIN `2019 Pre-Kindergarten Admissions Guide_pre_k_admissions_data` t3 ON t1.programname = t3.programname
  INNER JOIN `2019 Pre-Kindergarten Admissions Guide_pre_k_school_contact_info` t4 ON t2.phonenumber = t4.phonenumber
  INNER JOIN `node_5` t5 ON t4.address = t5.address
  WHERE t3.programtype = 'District School'
)
SELECT 
  dbn,
  programname,
  geodistrict,
  programtype,
  accessibility,
  address,
  additionalpriorities,
  extendedhoursallschools, geodistrict, languagesupports, languagesupportprograms
FROM ranked_data
WHERE row_num <= 3

detailed_results.query: Could you provide a breakdown of outdoor artworks by their exact location in the Public Design Commission Outdoor Public Art Inventory, using the latitude, longitude, and address from the main inventory, so I can see where each piece is situated? For each artwork, show when it was created and how it falls into general time categories (recent, mid‑century, or historic), and then, for every combination of that latitude, longitude, address, creation year, category, and borough, include how many pieces are at that spot and basic statistics on those creation years, such as the average year, the total, and the most recent year—only considering artworks where the material is specified.
detailed_results.sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (
  SELECT t1.latitude AS t1_latitude,
         t1.longitude AS t1_longitude,
         t1.address AS t1_address,
         t3.latitude,
         t3.longitude,
         t4.address,
         t3.date_created,
         t4.artwork_type1,
         t5.material,
         CASE
           WHEN t3.date_created > 2000 THEN 'recent'
           WHEN t3.date_created > 1950 THEN 'mid_century'
           ELSE 'historic'
         END AS category, t2.borough
  FROM `Public Design Commission Outdoor Public Art Inventory_outdoor_public_art_inventory_1` t1
  INNER JOIN `Public Design Commission Outdoor Public Art Inventory_outdoor_public_art_inventory` t2 ON t1.title = t2.title
  INNER JOIN `Public Design Commission Outdoor Public Art Inventory_outdoor_public_artworks_1` t3 ON t1.latitude = t3.latitude AND t1.longitude = t3.longitude
  INNER JOIN `Public Design Commission Outdoor Public Art Inventory_outdoor_public_art_inventory_2` t4 ON t1.address = t4.address
  INNER JOIN `Public Design Commission Outdoor Public Art Inventory_outdoor_public_artworks` t5 ON t2.acquisition = t5.acquisition
  WHERE t5.material IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT t1_latitude,
       t1_longitude,
       t1_address,
       date_created,
       category,
       COUNT(*) AS count,
       AVG(date_created) AS avg_value,
       SUM(date_created) AS total_value,
       MAX(date_created) AS max_value
FROM categorized_data
GROUP BY t1_latitude,
         t1_longitude,
         t1_address,
         date_created,
         category, borough

detailed_results.query: Could you show me, for each Bronx co-op property, where it's located (its coordinates and street address), how much income it's estimated to bring in overall, how much that works out to per square foot for the first comparable rental, and how these properties are categorized into low, medium, or high-income groups along with how many fall into each group and the average, total, and highest estimated income in each category at that address, grouped by the first comparable rental's gross income per square foot?
detailed_results.sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t1.latitude,
    t1.longitude,
    t1.bronx_cooperatives_comparable_properties_address,
    t3.bronx_cooperatives_comparable_properties_address AS t3_bronx_coop_address,
    t4.latitude AS t4_latitude,
    t4.longitude AS t4_longitude,
    t3.bronx_cooperatives_comparable_properties_est_gross_income,
    t4.bronx_cooperatives_comparable_properties_gross_income_per_sqft,
    t5.comparable_rental_1_gross_income_per_sqft,
    CASE
      WHEN t3.bronx_cooperatives_comparable_properties_est_gross_income > 2000000 THEN 'high income'
      WHEN t3.bronx_cooperatives_comparable_properties_est_gross_income > 1000000 THEN 'medium income'
      ELSE 'low income'
    END AS category, t2.comparable_rental_1_gross_income_per_sqft
  FROM `DOF： Cooperative Comparable Rental Income – Bronx – FY 2008 2009_bronx_coop_rental_comparables` t1
  INNER JOIN `DOF： Cooperative Comparable Rental Income – Bronx – FY 2008 2009_bronx_coop_rental_income` t2 
    ON t1.bronx_cooperatives_comparable_properties_boro_block_lot = t2.bronx_cooperatives_comparable_properties_boro_block_lot
  INNER JOIN `DOF： Cooperative Comparable Rental Income – Bronx – FY 2008 2009_bronx_coop_rental_comparisons` t3 
    ON t1.bronx_cooperatives_comparable_properties_address = t3.bronx_cooperatives_comparable_properties_address
  INNER JOIN `DOF： Cooperative Comparable Rental Income – Bronx – FY 2008 2009_bronx_rental_income_comparisons` t4 
    ON t1.latitude = t4.latitude AND t1.longitude = t4.longitude
  INNER JOIN `DOF： Cooperative Comparable Rental Income – Bronx – FY 2008 2009_bronx_coop_rental_income` t5 
    ON t2.bin = t5.bin
  WHERE t3.bronx_cooperatives_comparable_properties_est_gross_income IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
  bronx_cooperatives_comparable_properties_address,
  category,
  COUNT(*) AS count,
  AVG(bronx_cooperatives_comparable_properties_est_gross_income) AS avg_value,
  SUM(bronx_cooperatives_comparable_properties_est_gross_income) AS total_value,
  MAX(bronx_cooperatives_comparable_properties_est_gross_income) AS max_value
FROM categorized_data
GROUP BY 
  bronx_cooperatives_comparable_properties_address,
  category, comparable_rental_1_gross_income_per_sqft

detailed_results.sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (SELECT t1.school_name, t3.school_name, t1.attendance_rate, t1.college_career_rate, t3.pct_stu_safe, t5.grade9geapplicants3, CASE WHEN t1.attendance_rate > 0.9 THEN 'High attendance' WHEN t1.attendance_rate > 0.8 THEN 'Medium attendance' ELSE 'Low attendance' END as category, t2.school_10th_seats, t4.academicopportunities1 FROM `node_1` t1
INNER JOIN `2020 DOE High School Directory_high_school_admissions_data` t2 ON t1.dbn = t2.dbn
INNER JOIN `2020 DOE High School Directory_nyc_high_school_directory` t3 ON t1.school_name = t3.school_name
INNER JOIN `2020 DOE High School Directory_high_school_programs_info` t4 ON t2.code1 = t4.code1
INNER JOIN `2020 DOE High School Directory_high_school_admissions_data_1` t5 ON t4.fax_number = t5.fax_number WHERE t1.attendance_rate IS NOT NULL) SELECT school_name, category, COUNT(*) as count, AVG(attendance_rate) as avg_value, SUM(attendance_rate) as total_value, MAX(attendance_rate) as max_value FROM categorized_data GROUP BY school_name, category, school_10th_seats, academicopportunities1

detailed_results.query: Show, for the 2020 DOE High School Directory, each combination of admissions code, matching program code, t4 code, t4 fax number, fax number, high school program, admissions method, and eligibility, categorized as low, medium, or high demand based on the number of ninth grade general education applicants (only where that applicant count is present), and for each such group include the number of records, and the average, total, and highest applicant counts.
detailed_results.sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t2.code1,
    t4.code1 AS t4_code1,
    t4.fax_number AS t4_fax_number,
    t5.fax_number,
    t3.program1,
    t5.method1,
    t5.grade9geapplicants3,
    CASE 
      WHEN t5.grade9geapplicants3 > 50 THEN 'High Demand'
      WHEN t5.grade9geapplicants3 > 20 THEN 'Medium Demand'
      ELSE 'Low Demand'
    END AS category, t1.eligibility3
  FROM `node_1` t1
  INNER JOIN `2020 DOE High School Directory_high_school_admissions_data` t2 ON t1.dbn = t2.dbn
  INNER JOIN `2020 DOE High School Directory_nyc_high_school_directory` t3 ON t1.school_name = t3.school_name
  INNER JOIN `2020 DOE High School Directory_high_school_programs_info` t4 ON t2.code1 = t4.code1
  INNER JOIN `2020 DOE High School Directory_high_school_admissions_data_1` t5 ON t4.fax_number = t5.fax_number
  WHERE t5.grade9geapplicants3 IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
  code1,
  t4_code1,
  t4_fax_number,
  fax_number,
  program1,
  method1,
  category,
  COUNT(*) AS count,
  AVG(grade9geapplicants3) AS avg_value,
  SUM(grade9geapplicants3) AS total_value,
  MAX(grade9geapplicants3) AS max_value
FROM categorized_data
GROUP BY 
  code1,
  t4_code1,
  t4_fax_number,
  fax_number,
  program1,
  method1,
  category, eligibility3

detailed_results.query: Could you show me the top 50 high school program records in the 2020 DOE High School Directory, ranked by how many matching records they have, for each combination of school ID (DBN), school name, the program code (code1), the program name, and the admissions method used? Please only include records where there is a non‑null college and career readiness rate, and report the total count and average count of these matches for each DBN, school name, program code, program name, and admissions method.
detailed_results.sql:
WITH base_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t1.dbn,
    t1.school_name,
    t2.dbn AS t2_dbn,
    t2.code1,
    t3.school_name AS t3_school_name,
    t3.program1,
    t4.code1 AS t4_code1,
    t4.fax_number,
    t5.fax_number AS t5_fax_number,
    t5.method1
  FROM `node_1` t1
  INNER JOIN `2020 DOE High School Directory_high_school_admissions_data` t2 ON t1.dbn = t2.dbn
  INNER JOIN `2020 DOE High School Directory_nyc_high_school_directory` t3 ON t1.school_name = t3.school_name
  INNER JOIN `2020 DOE High School Directory_high_school_programs_info` t4 ON t2.code1 = t4.code1
  INNER JOIN `2020 DOE High School Directory_high_school_admissions_data_1` t5 ON t4.fax_number = t5.fax_number
  WHERE t1.college_career_rate IS NOT NULL
),
aggregated AS (
  SELECT 
    dbn,
    school_name,
    code1,
    program1,
    method1,
    COUNT(*) AS total,
    COUNT(*) AS count,
    AVG(COUNT(*)) OVER (PARTITION BY dbn, school_name, code1, program1, method1) AS average
  FROM base_data
  GROUP BY dbn, school_name, code1, program1, method1
)
SELECT 
  dbn,
  school_name,
  code1,
  program1,
  method1,
  total,
  count,
  average
FROM aggregated
WHERE total > 0
ORDER BY total DESC
LIMIT 50

detailed_results.sql:
WITH ranked_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t3.year,
    t3.axle2loadrating,
    t3.axle2space,
    t3.permittodate,
    t5.loadinweight,
    t5.loadoutweight,
    t5.applicationtypename,
    t5.industrytypename,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY t3.year 
      ORDER BY t5.loadoutweight DESC
    ) AS row_num, t1.axle3nooftires, t2.axle2weight, t4.registeredgvwr
  FROM `Annual Overweight Load (AOL) Permits_overweight_load_permits_2` t1
  INNER JOIN `Annual Overweight Load (AOL) Permits_overweight_load_permits_4` t2 ON t1.permitid = t2.permitid
  INNER JOIN `Annual Overweight Load (AOL) Permits_overweight_load_permits` t3 ON t1.fullpermitno = t3.fullpermitno
  INNER JOIN `Annual Overweight Load (AOL) Permits_overweight_load_permits_3` t4 ON t2.fullapplicationno = t4.fullapplicationno
  INNER JOIN `Annual Overweight Load (AOL) Permits_overweight_load_permits_1` t5 ON t4.oldpermitno = t5.oldpermitno
  WHERE t5.industrytypename IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
  year,
  axle2loadrating,
  axle2space,
  permittodate,
  loadinweight,
  loadoutweight,
  applicationtypename,
  industrytypename, axle3nooftires, axle2weight, registeredgvwr
FROM ranked_data
WHERE row_num <= 3

INNER JOIN `Annual Overweight Load (AOL) Permits_overweight_load_permits` t3 ON t1.fullpermitno = t3.fullpermitno
INNER JOIN `Annual Overweight Load (AOL) Permits_overweight_load_permits_3` t4 ON t2.fullapplicationno = t4.fullapplicationno
INNER JOIN `Annual Overweight Load (AOL) Permits_overweight_load_permits_1` t5 ON t4.oldpermitno = t5.oldpermitno GROUP BY t5.oldpermitno, t4.oldpermitno, t3.oldgrossvehicleweight, t3.permittodate, t4.permitapplication, t5.industrytypename, axle3nooftires, axle2weight

detailed_results.sql:
WITH ranked_data AS (SELECT t3.city_council_district, t3.total_units, t3.boiler_installation_date, t3.boiler_model, t5.of_res_units, t5.of_floors, t5.owner_telephone, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t3.city_council_district ORDER BY t3.total_units DESC) as row_num, t1.latitude, t2.boiler_age_range, t4.city_community_board FROM `NYC Clean Heat Dataset (Historical)_boiler_fuel_usage_records` t1
INNER JOIN `NYC Clean Heat Dataset (Historical)_nyc_boiler_compliance_data` t2 ON t1.dep_boiler_application = t2.dep_boiler_application
INNER JOIN `node_3` t3 ON t1.building_manager = t3.building_manager
INNER JOIN `NYC Clean Heat Dataset (Historical)_nyc_building_heating_data` t4 ON t2.owner = t4.owner
INNER JOIN `NYC Clean Heat Dataset (Historical)_nyc_building_ownership_info` t5 ON t4.borough_block_lot = t5.borough_block_lot WHERE t3.total_units IS NOT NULL) SELECT city_council_district, total_units, boiler_installation_date, boiler_model, of_res_units, of_floors, owner_telephone, latitude, boiler_age_range, city_community_board FROM ranked_data WHERE row_num <= 5

detailed_results.query: For the NYC Clean Heat Dataset (Historical), for every combination of the building manager listed in the boiler fuel usage records and the building manager listed in the related node_3 building data, can you show me, by city_council_district, total_units in the building, of_res_units value indicating how many of those units are residential, boiler_age_range, and city_community_board, how many records fall into each category based on total_gallons_high, along with the average, total, and maximum total_gallons_high?
detailed_results.sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t1.building_manager AS t1_building_manager,
    t3.building_manager AS t3_building_manager,
    t1.total_gallons_high,
    t3.city_council_district,
    t3.total_units,
    t5.of_res_units,
    CASE 
      WHEN t1.total_gallons_high > 150000 THEN 'very_high_usage'
      WHEN t1.total_gallons_high > 50000 THEN 'high_usage'
      ELSE 'moderate_or_low_usage'
    END AS category, t2.boiler_age_range, t4.city_community_board
  FROM `NYC Clean Heat Dataset (Historical)_boiler_fuel_usage_records` t1
  INNER JOIN `NYC Clean Heat Dataset (Historical)_nyc_boiler_compliance_data` t2 ON t1.dep_boiler_application = t2.dep_boiler_application
  INNER JOIN `node_3` t3 ON t1.building_manager = t3.building_manager
  INNER JOIN `NYC Clean Heat Dataset (Historical)_nyc_building_heating_data` t4 ON t2.owner = t4.owner
  INNER JOIN `NYC Clean Heat Dataset (Historical)_nyc_building_ownership_info` t5 ON t4.borough_block_lot = t5.borough_block_lot
  WHERE t3.total_units IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
  t1_building_manager,
  t3_building_manager,
  city_council_district,
  total_units,
  of_res_units,
  category,
  COUNT(*) AS count,
  AVG(total_gallons_high) AS avg_value,
  SUM(total_gallons_high) AS total_value,
  MAX(total_gallons_high) AS max_value
FROM categorized_data
GROUP BY 
  t1_building_manager,
  t3_building_manager,
  city_council_district,
  total_units,
  of_res_units,
  category, boiler_age_range, city_community_board

detailed_results.query: Could you show me, for each property, the top three buildings with the highest number of units, including who manages the building (from both management records if they differ), the full property identifier used by the city (from both building heating and ownership records), how many units there are in total, when the boiler was installed, the boiler's heating capacity, how many of the units are residential, and the boiler's age range?
detailed_results.sql:
WITH ranked_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t1.building_manager,
    t3.building_manager AS t3_building_manager,
    t4.borough_block_lot,
    t5.borough_block_lot AS t5_borough_block_lot,
    t3.total_units,
    t3.boiler_installation_date,
    t4.boiler_capacity_gross_btu,
    t5.of_res_units,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t4.borough_block_lot ORDER BY t3.total_units DESC) AS row_num, t2.boiler_age_range
  FROM `NYC Clean Heat Dataset (Historical)_boiler_fuel_usage_records` t1
  INNER JOIN `NYC Clean Heat Dataset (Historical)_nyc_boiler_compliance_data` t2 ON t1.dep_boiler_application = t2.dep_boiler_application
  INNER JOIN `node_3` t3 ON t1.building_manager = t3.building_manager
  INNER JOIN `NYC Clean Heat Dataset (Historical)_nyc_building_heating_data` t4 ON t2.owner = t4.owner
  INNER JOIN `NYC Clean Heat Dataset (Historical)_nyc_building_ownership_info` t5 ON t4.borough_block_lot = t5.borough_block_lot
  WHERE t3.total_units IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
  building_manager,
  t3_building_manager,
  borough_block_lot,
  t5_borough_block_lot,
  total_units,
  boiler_installation_date,
  boiler_capacity_gross_btu,
  of_res_units, boiler_age_range
FROM ranked_data
WHERE row_num <= 3

WITH categorized_data AS (SELECT t2.owner as t2_owner, t4.owner as t4_owner, t4.borough_block_lot as t4_borough_block_lot, t5.borough_block_lot as t5_borough_block_lot, t3.total_units, t5.of_res_units, t4.boiler_capacity_gross_btu, CASE WHEN t4.boiler_capacity_gross_btu > 5000000 THEN 'large capacity' WHEN t4.boiler_capacity_gross_btu > 1000000 THEN 'medium capacity' ELSE 'small capacity' END as category, t1.latitude FROM `NYC Clean Heat Dataset (Historical)_boiler_fuel_usage_records` t1
INNER JOIN `NYC Clean Heat Dataset (Historical)_nyc_boiler_compliance_data` t2 ON t1.dep_boiler_application = t2.dep_boiler_application
INNER JOIN `node_3` t3 ON t1.building_manager = t3.building_manager
INNER JOIN `NYC Clean Heat Dataset (Historical)_nyc_building_heating_data` t4 ON t2.owner = t4.owner
INNER JOIN `NYC Clean Heat Dataset (Historical)_nyc_building_ownership_info` t5 ON t4.borough_block_lot = t5.borough_block_lot WHERE t4.boiler_capacity_gross_btu IS NOT NULL) SELECT t2_owner, t4_owner, t4_borough_block_lot, t5_borough_block_lot, total_units, of_res_units, category, COUNT(*) as count, AVG(boiler_capacity_gross_btu) as avg_value, SUM(boiler_capacity_gross_btu) as total_value, MAX(boiler_capacity_gross_btu) as max_value FROM categorized_data GROUP BY t2_owner, t4_owner, t4_borough_block_lot, t5_borough_block_lot, total_units, of_res_units, category, latitude
